einzeiler: Sarah Hepola explores the untold stories of the original Dallas Cowboys Cheerleaders.
kurzfassung: Sarah Hepola investigates the history of the original Dallas Cowboys Cheerleaders squad, which debuted in 1972. Despite their global popularity, the voices of the women themselves have largely been missing from the narrative. Across eight episodes, the podcast examines the squad's cultural impact, controversies, and the complexities of women's bodies and value.
stichpunkte: Sarah Hepola visits the site of Texas Stadium and reflects on growing up seeing the Dallas Cowboys Cheerleaders.
Buzzil Baker, one of the original seven cheerleaders, describes walking down the tunnel and introducing something entirely new to football.
The squad became known as America's sweethearts, combining pageant beauty, etiquette, and sex appeal.
Despite fifty years as a global sensation, the actual voices of the cheerleaders have largely been absent from the mainstream story.
The origin of the iconic uniform stems from imagination.
The podcast series explores the legacy of the cheerleaders, addressing the policing of women's bodies and behavior, major lawsuits, and cultural changes.
beschreibung: The original Dallas Cowboys Cheerleaders squad burst onto the field back in 1972—the same year Title IX passed, the same year Deep Throat came out, and a year before Roe v. Wade. Sarah Hepola digs into the untold stories behind the global pop culture phenomenon, from the stripper who allegedly inspired the squad’s creation, to a scandalous Playboy cover shoot that was partly a battle over fair wages, to the ongoing debate about sexuality and women’s bodies in a post-#MeToo world. The result is a vibrant mix of history, cultural criticism, and storytelling, featuring interviews with New Yorker writer Jia Tolentino, award-winning novelist Ben Fountain, Oscar-nominated director Dana Adam Shapiro, local television sports legend Dale Hansen, folk-writing hero Joe Nick Patoski, and a whole bunch of cheerleaders whose names you don’t know yet—but should.
